fluff.overview:
The Black Lanner was developed by Clan Jade Falcon in 3052, born from the hard lessons of the Placement Trials that determined which Clans would participate in Operation REVIVAL. Designed as a fast medium OmniMech capable of filling multiple tactical roles, the fifty-five-ton chassis sacrificed pod space in favor of raw speed, mounting an engine that consumed almost half its total mass. Initial production delays at the Ironhold Alpha Complex meant the Black Lanner missed the opening waves of the invasion entirely, arriving in the Inner Sphere only when the Falcon Khans returned from Strana Mechty after the election of ilKhan Ulric Kerensky.

Named after a transplanted Terran avian introduced to Ironhold, the Black Lanner first proved its worth during the Battle of Tukayyid, where two Stars of the new design served as fire-support elements in light reconnaissance formations. Production later expanded to Olivetti Weaponry on Sudeten, a captured Lyran factory refitted for Clan manufacturing, ensuring continued supply as tensions with the Homeworld Clans mounted.
fluff.capabilities:
The Black Lanner's primary strength lies in its extraordinary speed. A massive 385-rated extralight fusion engine paired with an integral MASC system allows the chassis to reach sustained speeds of 118 kilometers per hour, with bursts exceeding 151 kilometers per hour, fast enough to outrun many light 'Mechs half its size. This performance comes at considerable cost, however, as the engine alone consumes nearly half the design's tonnage, leaving a mere thirteen tons of pod space for weaponry and equipment. Where most medium OmniMechs in the fifty-five-ton range boast substantially heavier firepower, the Black Lanner trades raw hitting power for unmatched mobility in its weight class.

A JF 5 Light Endo Steel chassis and eight tons of Compound JF Ferro-Fibrous armor maximize protection within the tight weight budget, while the Stable design quirk provides reliable weapon platform characteristics even at high speed. The primary configuration exemplifies the design's versatility, mounting an ER large laser and LRM-10 for ranged engagements alongside paired ER medium lasers and an SRM-6 for close combat, with an ECM suite providing electronic protection.

The Black Lanner truly excels when operating in mixed formations with lighter 'Mechs. Paired with Fire Falcons or Fire Moths acting as spotters and harassers, the Black Lanner exploits flushed targets with decisive strikes, a synergistic hunting relationship deliberately modeled on the cooperative behavior of the native fire falcon and introduced black lanner bird species on Ironhold.
fluff.history:
The Black Lanner emerged from Clan Jade Falcon's critical self-assessment following the Placement Trials for Operation REVIVAL. Recognizing gaps in their touman's medium-weight OmniMech capabilities, Falcon scientists designed a chassis optimized for speed and tactical flexibility over brute force. Production began at the Ironhold Alpha Complex on the Jade Falcon homeworld, though delays with initial models prevented the design from participating in the early invasion waves. The Black Lanner finally reached the Inner Sphere when the Falcon Khans returned from electing ilKhan Ulric Kerensky on Strana Mechty, carrying two Stars of the new OmniMech as part of their re-supply contingent.

Assigned as fire-support units in light reconnaissance Stars, the Black Lanner quickly proved its worth during the Battle of Tukayyid. Since that initial deployment, the design has remained primarily a Jade Falcon asset, though Clan Ice Hellion and Clan Steel Viper acquired sizable numbers through the numerous clashes and Trials that characterized inter-Clan relations in the post-Tukayyid era. The Steel Vipers in particular obtained several Black Lanners during their conflicts with the Falcons, with some of these machines later changing hands again during the Falcon-Viper War.

Despite its popularity among Jade Falcon warriors, the Black Lanner has always been a relatively rare sight in the Falcon touman. To reduce reliance on distant Homeworld supply lines, the Jade Falcons expanded production to Olivetti Weaponry on Sudeten, a former Lyran Commonwealth factory captured during the invasion. After extensive refitting, Olivetti first produced the second-line Spirit in 3063, then expanded to frontline OmniMechs including the Fire Falcon, Black Lanner, and Turkina within a year. This Inner Sphere production proved prescient when rising tensions between the Jade Falcons and the Home Clans led to the cessation of all Black Lanner production in Clan Space by 3068, during the opening stages of the Wars of Reaving.

The Jihad inflicted further damage on the Sudeten production line, causing the Black Lanner's already limited numbers to dwindle further. Many surviving examples became pre-Jihad veterans, maintained and repaired rather than replaced. A renewed push to increase production at Olivetti Weaponry was vindicated by the Jade Falcons' preliminary success on Coventry in February 3148, where a strike force led by Galaxy Commander Stephanie Chistu deployed several Black Lanners against the Seventeenth Arcturan Guards. During fighting in the Ridesein River Valley, Black Lanner T configurations used plasma cannons to overheat heavier Lyran 'Mechs while their lighter partners cut the disabled targets down. In a later engagement, Star Colonel Rose Faulk of the Fifth Battle Cluster dispatched a mixed Star of Black Lanners, Fire Falcons, and a Fire Moth to pursue a fleeing Lyran lance carrying valuable intelligence, employing traditional cooperative hunting tactics to run the enemy down and secure the intel.

The renewed interest in manufacturing the Black Lanner in larger quantities has met with enthusiasm from Jade Falcon light 'Mech pilots, who know from long experience that their Stars claim more kills when fighting alongside the fast-striking OmniMech. Warriors continue to insist on pairing Black Lanners with Fire Falcons in particular, maintaining a tactical doctrine that dates back to the design's earliest deployments and reflects the symbiotic hunting behavior for which it was named.
fluff.deployment: A mixed-technology configuration that incorporates Inner Sphere components alongside Clan systems, the I variant mounts a medium variable speed pulse laser in the right arm for adaptable direct fire, paired with two ER medium lasers in the left arm. Three heavy machine guns in the right torso provide anti-infantry capability, while a Streak SRM-4 in the left torso adds guided missile support. A targeting computer enhances accuracy across all weapon systems, making this skirmisher configuration particularly effective in the hands of pilots who favor precise, calculated engagements over raw volume of fire.
